easy.def: To cut a picture into glass or metal.
examples: She will etch her name.
The artist etched the glass.
Names were etched in stone.

more.def: To cut a design into a hard surface, such as glass or metal.
examples: The artist etched a design into the glass.
Names were etched on the old stone.
He etched his name on the trophy.
The mountain seems eternal.
They shared eternal friendship.
The stars seem eternal.

more.def: Without a beginning or end, lasting forever.
examples: The old mountain seemed eternal.
The two friends promised eternal loyalty.
The story spoke of eternal love.
It felt like an eternity.
Eternity has no end.
We waited an eternity.

more.def: Time without end, or a very long time.
examples: The wait felt like an eternity.
Some people believe in life for all eternity.
It took an eternity for the bus to come.
An ethereal glow.
The ethereal music.
An ethereal figure.

more.def: Extremely light and delicate, almost not of this world.
examples: An ethereal glow lit the misty lake.
The ethereal music floated through the hall.
The fairy had an ethereal beauty.

easy.def: A rule about what is right and wrong.
examples: She has a strong work ethic.
Ethics are about being good.
Honesty is an ethic.

more.def: A set of ideas about what is right and wrong, or a way of behaving that is believed to be good.
examples: She has a strong work ethic and always tries her best.
Honesty is an important ethic in our school.
The class talked about ethics and fair play.
It is ethical to be honest.
That was an ethical choice.
She made an ethical decision.

more.def: Following what is right and fair, and being honest and good in the way you act.
examples: It is ethical to return a wallet that you find on the street.
The scientists made an ethical choice to protect the animals.
She believed it was ethical to share the credit with her team.

easy.def: Having to do with a group that shares customs, food and language.
examples: We ate ethnic food.
An ethnic festival.
The ethnic group.

more.def: Having to do with a group of people who share the same culture, language, food and traditions.
examples: The town held an ethnic festival with music, dancing and food from many cultures.
We tried ethnic food at the new restaurant.
The ethnic group celebrates with special songs.
We learned table etiquette.
Good etiquette is polite.
Etiquette matters.

more.def: The rules for polite and proper behavior in a society or a situation.
examples: Good table etiquette means chewing with your mouth closed.
We learned about phone etiquette, such as saying hello politely.
It is good etiquette to say thank you.
